study.title: Deep neural networks for ECG-free cardiac phase and end-diastolic frame detection on coronary angiographies

imaging.modality_detail: Invasive X-ray coronary angiography (cine), frames resampled to 512x512 and to 10 fps
imaging.frames_per_sequence: Acquisitions at 7.5-30 fps; model input windows of 10 frames (1 s at 10 fps); 95.1 +/- 14.9 frames per angiography in the secondary set

data_released.detail: Data cannot be made public due to GDPR regulations and informed consent

annotation.annotator_expertise: Experienced clinical examiners annotated R and T peaks on ECG for a validation subset; training labels derived automatically from ECG; vessel centrelines manually annotated for the vesselness model

task.task_description: ECG-free frame-level cardiac phase (systole/diastole) classification and end-diastolic frame detection on coronary angiographies, with a vesselness segmentation network preselecting frames with well visible arteries
task.clinical_application: Automated EDF selection for 3D QCA and image-based FFR, and cardiac phase identification without ECG

architecture_names: Spatial CNN + temporal CNN cardiac phase predictor

temporal_evidence.quote: A second CNN performs temporal convolutions on this matrix, independently for all 64 image features.

evaluation.external_validation_detail: Trained on 56,655 angiographies from 6820 patients; main evaluation on 20,780 angiographies from 6261 patients acquired at a different clinical site; additional expert-annotated subset (207 angiographies) and secondary dataset (175 angiographies, 84 patients)

G1.quote: past methods cannot be directly applied on our data for performance comparison

G2.quote: the training / validation and evaluation datasets were acquired at different clinical sites

G3.quote: it takes as input sequences of 10 frames from the preselected frame interval, performs spatial and temporal convolutions

G5.quote: This strategy allowed us to reduce drastically the annotation costs

G10.quote: cannot be made public, considering GDPR regulations and the content of the informed consent signed by the patients

other_limitations: Reduced confidence and accuracy under panning (table movement)
Suboptimal performance with total occlusions or few visible arteries
ECG-angiography desynchronization (e.g. conduction disorders) affects ECG-derived ground truth
No access to patient characteristics or diagnoses for the main evaluation dataset
T peaks not always reliably detectable on ECG signals
